name: CA-20
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Vince Fong with a massive fundraising advantage ($1.85M vs ~$17K)
No polling or expert ratings; fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: The R+16 lean, Fong's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing him at 98% all point to a safe Republican hold; the challenger has raised almost nothing. The forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied margin with no evidence to move it.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or late outside spending against Fong is the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
CA-20 is a heavily Republican Central Valley seat where incumbent Vince Fong is seeking another term. The district's partisan lean of R+16 makes a Democratic win a steep climb under any conditions. Fong has raised about $1.85 million and holds over $450,000 in cash, while Democrat Sandra Van Scotter has raised roughly $17,000 and shows negative cash on hand, leaving her with no visible means to compete.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Fong at 98 percent. With that lopsided financial picture and no signs of a competitive environment, the seat is rated Safe Republican.
